newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Armoured carriers protect Cambodian co-premier.
newsitem.headline: Armoured carriers protect Cambodian co-premier.

text.p: Four armoured personnel carriers rolled through the Cambodian capital on Friday to beef up security at the house of co-Premier Hun Sen as political tensions appeared to be worsening after a deadly grenade attack.

Reuters reporters saw four armoured vehicles pass down a main boulevard, turn down the street where opposition leader Sam Rainsy's Khmer Nation Party (KNP) is headquartered and pull into Hun Sen's compound.
"They are here to protect Hun Sen," a soldier said.
On Thursday, Hun Sen had said police were investigating two suspects for allegedly plotting to assassinate members of his family, his friends and staff.
His comments came after four grenades ripped through a demonstration led by Sam Rainsy last Sunday in the worst political violence in years, killing as many as 19 and wounding more than 100.

Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury, has accused Hun Sen of being behind the attack. Hun Sen has denied responsibility and condemned the violence but suggested that the protest leaders should be arrested.
Hun Sen and co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who formed an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, have agreed on an investigation by the Interior Ministry.
But Ranariddh, U.N. officials and parliamentarian Kem Sokha have expressed doubts justice would be served by the ministry.
Joining the chorus on Friday were hardliners from the rebel Khmer Rouge, who urged the international community to investigate the grenade attack.
